metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights Michigan | Antrim & Statewide
metaDescription: Sell your Michigan mineral rights to a direct buyer who reads your actual production before quoting a number. No mailbox pressure, no flat offers.
heroLead: You own a piece of ground in the Antrim trend, or somewhere else in Michigan, and you're trying to figure out what it's actually worth. Let's start there instead of a form letter.
intro: If you've got a mailbox full of offers on Michigan mineral rights, you already know the pattern: a flat number, a deadline, and no mention of your actual well. We work differently. We look at your real production history, your decline stage, and current gas prices before we ever quote a figure, and we'll tell you exactly how we got there.

sections.heading: Michigan minerals aren't like everywhere else
paragraphs: The Antrim Shale is biogenic gas, and it behaves differently than the plays that dominate national headlines. Wells decline sharply in their first several years, then settle into a long, shallow tail that can keep producing small volumes for decades. A well twenty years into that tail is a different asset than a well two years in, even if both show up on a check stub every month, and that difference should drive the number, not get glossed over by it.

Ownership out here is often just as tangled as the geology. A lot of tracts trace back to farms broken up among heirs two or three generations ago, and by the time it lands on your desk, you might own a fraction of a fraction with a legal description written before the county had paved roads through it. We work with that reality instead of pretending it's simple.

sections.heading: How we price an offer
paragraphs: If your minerals are producing, we start with your division order or recent royalty statements, look at where the well sits on its decline curve, and apply a multiple tied to recent income, adjusted for current commodity prices and how much production life is realistically left. If your minerals are undeveloped, we look at drilling and lease activity in your specific county, and we're upfront that a tract with no production history carries more uncertainty in the number.
What we won't do is quote you a flat per-acre figure without asking a single question about your tract. That's how mailbox offers work, and it's not how a real appraisal works.

sections.heading: No pressure, no games
paragraphs: We don't put expiration dates on our offers, and we're comfortable if you shop our number against another buyer. If leasing makes more sense for your situation than selling outright, we'll tell you that too, rather than push a sale that doesn't fit what you actually need.

sections.heading: Inherited a fraction and not sure where to start
paragraphs: Most of the people we talk to didn't buy their minerals, they inherited a piece of a farm that's been in the family for generations, often split between siblings, cousins, or an estate that never got fully sorted out. If that's you, you're not behind, that's just how mineral ownership usually works out here. We can help trace the deed history, confirm your fractional share through county records, and figure out what it's actually worth before you decide anything.
You don't need a folder of paperwork to start the conversation. A rough sense of the county and how you came to own the interest is enough to get moving.

sections.heading: Producing or undeveloped, either way we'll talk
paragraphs: Some of the tracts we look at are under wells that have been paying royalties for twenty years, deep into their Antrim tail. Others have never had a well drilled on them at all. Both are worth a conversation, though the valuation approach and the amount of certainty involved differ quite a bit between the two, and we'll be upfront with you about which situation you're in and what that means for the number.

sections.heading: Talk it through before you decide anything
paragraphs: You don't have to know already whether you want to sell, lease, or hold. Plenty of the calls we take are from owners who just want to understand their situation better, whether that's reading a confusing royalty statement, comparing leasing against selling, or figuring out what a fair number would even look like for their tract. There's no cost or obligation attached to asking.

faqs.question: Do you buy undeveloped mineral rights or only producing ones?
faqs.answer: Yes, though undeveloped tracts are valued differently, leaning on lease activity and drilling interest nearby rather than production history.

faqs.question: What areas of Michigan do you buy in?
faqs.answer: We focus on the Antrim trend, including Otsego, Antrim, Kalkaska, Montmorency, and Grand Traverse counties, along with mineral interests elsewhere in the state.

faqs.question: How is my offer calculated?
faqs.answer: For producing minerals, it's built from your recent royalty income and the well's decline stage. For undeveloped acreage, it reflects nearby drilling and lease activity, with more inherent uncertainty in the number.

faqs.question: Do I have to sell my entire interest?
faqs.answer: No, you can sell a portion of your mineral interest and keep the rest, depending on what fits your situation.

faqs.question: Is there any obligation to get a number from you?
faqs.answer: No, requesting an offer costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything. Compare it against another buyer if you'd like before deciding.
